answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding, with a public challenge window: if peers prove duplicated control or fabricated work, a verifier slashes the bond and pays the challenger. The bond stays locked per concurrently active identity, so an attacker splitting into basalt, vine, and island accounts must tie up capital for each; reusing one bond means those accounts cannot act at once. This raises the cost of Sybils, though it cannot eliminate them.
